candidate.perspective: Australian electricity-system planners and industrial electricity users evaluating the existing renewable generation base and its usable access, not commodity investors.
candidate.structural_condition: An expanding domestic solar-and-wind electricity production base coexists with declining physical energy-export volumes, creating distinct domestic flexibility and export-dependence questions.
candidate.delta: The ABS Energy Account released 29 October 2026 documents 2024–25 renewable electricity supply of 372 PJ (+9.7%, from 339 PJ), 37% of domestic electricity use (34% previously), while physical energy exports fell 3.1% to 17,363 PJ, their lowest in a decade. This is newly published retrospective evidence, not evidence of a new 2026 commissioning.
candidate.mechanism: From the electricity-user perspective, already produced renewable electricity may be leveraged for domestic loads and decarbonisation if network access, time-of-day availability and storage/flexibility permit; declining coal/LNG/other physical export volumes represent a separate external-market exposure, not a direct transfer of export energy into the grid. Export energy totals and renewable electricity use have different denominators and must not be subtracted or compared as a single balance.
catalysts: Evidence of 2025–26 renewable commissioning and usable transmission capacity rather than annual energy-account inference alone.
Measured curtailment, grid congestion, firming capacity and industrial offtake under accessible connection rules.
Updated 2025–26 export energy volumes and energy-price exposure.
candidate.invalidation: A revised ABS series reverses the renewable/export divergence, or updated system-operation data show that renewable supply cannot be economically accessed by the named users without prohibitive network or firming costs.

evidence.name: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Energy Account Australia 2024–25, 29 October 2026
Australian Bureau of Statistics, Energy exports at 10-year low, 29 October 2026

research_note: Discovery-only candidate; new statistical evidence describes FY2024–25, not an October 2026 operational transition. No inferred project economics, asset returns, access right or canonical Atlas promotion.
